- When sentiment turns negative or shows strong downward momentum, reduce forecasted price by 5–10% to account for risk aversion.  
- If sentiment spikes upward with high news volume, model tends to overreact — cap forecast peak at 10–15% above recent high.  
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots — apply a 3–5 day mean-reversion correction downward.  
- If sentiment is flat or mildly positive but news volume is low, model overestimates — reduce forecast by 3–7% to reflect muted market activity.  
- When sentiment shows strong upward trend over 3–5 days, model tends to lag — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% per day of sentiment momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative for 3+ consecutive days, model often fails to correct — apply a 5–10% downward bias to avoid “overconfidence” in recovery.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate volatility — smooth forecast by reducing standard deviation by 15–20% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
